articles.title: Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma's day out in Auckland: Booming drives, plenty of edges and high intensity
articles.summary: AUCKLAND: A handful of cars were still lining up for the \"boot sale\" in the Eden Park compound when Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma arrived at the venue to
articles.body: AUCKLAND: A handful of cars were still lining up for the "boot sale" in the Eden Park compound when Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma arrived at the venue to continue their ODI preparations. It was a perfect day for cricket: the temperature hovered around 20 degrees, the sun was out in all its glory, and a gentle breeze provided a pleasant balance. This was the experienced duo's second net session, and both Kohli and Rohit hit the ground running as soon as they arrived.After a quick stretch with the resistance band, India's No.3 was down to business on the centre wicket at the training ground and faced a few throwdowns before taking guard against Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Anshul Kamboj. The morning freshness set-up the session nicely and the troika instantly hit the right areas, keeping the two stalwarts on their toes throughout their hit.Nabi, in particular, used the breeze to his advantage, getting nice shape going away from the two right-handers and kept flirting with the outside edges of Rohit and Kohli. There was no respite from the other end with Brar hitting the right length and Kamboj getting a fair few deliveries moving both ways. While Kohli grew in confidence with his trademark cover-drives, none intended to graze the lush green outfield, whereas Rohit remained a bit tentative outside the off-stump.The two veterans were very comfortable playing deliveries off their pads but it wasn't the case when Nabi got a few to nip back from the spot he was gently curving away for most of the session. The 29-year-old, who is now part of the ODI squad for the first three ODIs, enjoyed top rhythm during his one-hour spell, and the relentlessness of Kamboj and Brar certainly helped.Intent the keyword for KohliAmidst the nicks and frustration of missing the drives, Kohli didn't compromise on intent. Most of the drives were uppish and he kept searching for the trademark whip towards mid-wicket. Even when Rohit finished his session and was resting by the ice box, Kohli gestured to a waiting KL Rahul for one last dance.He pulled, drove, flicked, cut and lofted it out of the park with sheer disdain.The drill lasted close to ten minutes and one hit out of the ground got the local bowlers, who were loosening up in the gym, on their feet. When Kohli was done batting, he placed two cones and did multiple high-intensity sprints to cap off a productive day.Karan Aujla query by RohitYou can't keep Karan Aujla out of the social media feeds these days and Rohit too seemed caught up with the trend when he went for a quick restroom break. The two local cricketers got excited when the former Indian captain entered the area and when they politely requested for a picture, they were a bit taken aback by his simplicity and the query."You boys are Aujla fans," Rohit quipped before posing for the two who smiled ear-to-ear after getting the perfect picture for the 'gram!. No prizes for guessing the song. "Ashke," the unannounced anthem of the nation these days, would have been the unanimous choice.Gill absent; Rahul, Ruturaj trainIndia ODI captain Shubman Gill wasn't present for the nets and it's understood he had a scheduled gym session during that period. Rahul and Ruturaj Gaikwad, who joined the team on October 31, had an extended hit divided between the nets and the centre wicket.From the support staff, spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule and fielding coach Shubhadeep Ghosh were in attendance alongwith Dayanand Garani and Nuwan Seneviratne. The rest remained with India's T20I team for the final match of the series in Hamilton.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I was just waiting for that moment': Fakhar Zaman after Pakistan match India's 2002 Lord's record
articles.summary: Fakhar Zaman had gone through four matches without the kind of performance he wanted.
articles.body: Fakhar Zaman had gone through four matches without the kind of performance he wanted. But the Pakistan opener knew that a big innings was around the corner. He just had to wait for the right moment. That moment arrived in the One-Day International tri-series final against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday. Zaman smashed 127 off 99 balls to help Pakistan chase down 326 and win the final by three wickets.Pakistan finished at 331 for seven in 48.3 overs, with nine balls to spare. It was a special victory for the hosts, who also equalled India's famous record for the highest successful chase in an ODI final.Speaking after winning the Player of the Match award, Zaman explained how he dealt with his lack of runs in the previous four matches and why he never changed his approach.'I was just waiting for that moment'Zaman admitted that he was not at his best at the start of the final. However, he continued to trust his preparation and believed that a big score would come when he found his rhythm."No, look, I've played enough cricket now to know that when it's my day and the ball starts coming nicely off my bat, I'll score big. So I was just waiting for that moment. I didn't do anything particularly different from the way I had approached the previous four matches. I prepared for this game in exactly the same way. But that's the thing: when you score runs, we start talking about how mentally ready you were, how your fitness was and all of that. I prepared for this match in the same way I had prepared for the other games. Luckily, the runs came today," Zaman said.The left-hander also spoke about his struggles at the beginning of the innings and how important the century was for him."Look, the way my first four matches had gone, I felt a good performance was due, and I was putting in the effort. But cricket is such a game that sometimes you're in really good touch, but the runs just don't come. Even today, I was struggling a little at the start, but luckily the runs came, and that's a good thing for me. Whenever there is a final, I seem to score runs," he said.Pakistan were in trouble early in the chase after Dilshan Madushanka dismissed Babar Azam for a five-ball duck. The Sri Lankan pacer also picked up another wicket in the powerplay.Zaman then joined Saad Baig, and the two rebuilt the innings with a 149-run partnership.Baig scored 74 off 75 balls, registering his maiden ODI half-century. Zaman said his young teammate's approach allowed him to take his time at the other end."I've played domestic cricket with him as well, and he's a very talented player. Even today, when I was struggling at that stage, he came in and scored quite quickly. That allowed me to relax and take my time. If he had also played slowly like me, perhaps I would have tried to take a few more chances, and if you take those chances, you can end up losing your wicket. So the credit goes to him for the way he started and the way he built his innings. In my opinion, his was the best innings of the match," Zaman said.Pakistan match India's famous 2002 Lord's recordZaman's century helped Pakistan complete the joint-highest successful chase in an ODI final. Pakistan's chase of 326 was level with India's famous run chase against England in the 2002 NatWest Series final at Lord's.India had also chased down 326 to win by two wickets. Mohammad Kaif scored an unbeaten 87, while Yuvraj Singh contributed 69. The two played a major role in taking India out of trouble before Kaif and Zaheer Khan completed the job in a thrilling finish.More than two decades later, Pakistan matched that achievement with their own memorable chase.Minhas and Nawaz take Pakistan homeZaman's dismissal for 127 and Salman Agha's departure for 17 left Pakistan at 230 for five. However, Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz put together a 94-run partnership to take the hosts close to victory.Minhas scored a valuable half-century and helped Pakistan cross the finish line with nine balls remaining.Earlier, Sri Lanka had posted 325 for eight, thanks to Kamindu Mendis' 131 off 128 balls and Pavan Rathnayake's 77. The pair added 146 runs for the third wicket.Pakistan's bowlers fought back in the final overs, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking two wickets for 50 runs.'The happiness is even greater'For Zaman, scoring runs in a final and helping his team lift the trophy made the occasion even more special."Absolutely. Look, whatever performances you put in throughout the tournament, you do them with the aim of winning the trophy. And when you score runs in the final, the happiness is even greater. I consider myself lucky that I managed to score runs in the final today," he said.The victory gave Pakistan their first ODI tri-series title since 2008, when they defeated India in the Kitply Cup final in Bangladesh. It also helped them make amends for their defeat to New Zealand in the final of the home tri-series in 2025.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'There will be some changes': Pat Cummins hints at Test shake-up after South Africa defeat
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins admitted that the team could make changes after South Africa beat them by 176 runs in the third Test at Newlands on
articles.body: Australia captain Pat Cummins admitted that the team could make changes after South Africa beat them by 176 runs in the third Test at Newlands on Saturday, sealing the series 2-1.It was Australia's second successive defeat in the series, with South Africa also moving past them to the top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings."I still think we're a really good side," Cummins told journalists. "Playing the now number one side in their own country we had our moments in every Test."However, Cummins acknowledged that Australia would need to assess whether changes were required as they prepare for a busy schedule of Test cricket over the next year."We'll be asking those questions internally as well," he said. "We need to get better if we want to get back to number one. Maybe there will be some changes in style, changes in the personnel."Cummins said Australia's chances of chasing the target of 288 were hit hard when Kagiso Rabada took two wickets in the first over of the innings. Rabada picked up another wicket in his opening spell, removing Australia's top three batters and leaving the visitors with a difficult task.Australia were eventually bowled out for 111, with off-spinner Simon Harmer taking a career-best six for 16 in 21.1 overs.South Africa captain Temba Bavuma said the series victory reflected the character of his team. He pointed to the fourth-day partnership between centurions Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder, saying it showed the team's ability to fight back after being behind in the match for the first three days."When the batters did what they did, the bowlers had the confidence. The way Rabada started today he got everything going. From then on we were able to keep a tight grip on things."Bavuma also said Harmer's performance, which earned him the Player of the Match award with figures of 10 for 120, underlined the strength of South Africa's bowling attack."It's been the backbone of our team," said Bavuma. "It's been a big part of why we've been successful. When the wicket suits the fast bowlers, we have the guys. And when the spinners come into the game, we also have that ability."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Un-Australian, disgraceful, immature': Warner, Waugh tear into Australia after series defeat
articles.summary: Australia are facing growing calls for changes following their batting collapse against South Africa in the third Test, with former opener David Warner
articles.body: Australia are facing growing calls for changes following their batting collapse against South Africa in the third Test, with former opener David Warner leading the criticism of what he described as "utterly disgraceful" batting.Chasing 288 on the fifth day at Newlands in Cape Town, Australia were bowled out for 111. The defeat not only cost them the Test but also saw them lose the series 2-1 after taking a 1-0 lead.The result also saw defending world champions South Africa move above Australia to the top of the International Cricket Council's Test rankings.Australia had entered the series with questions over an ageing team, particularly their bowling attack comprising Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon. Those concerns followed a surprise nine-wicket defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin in August.However, it was Australia's batting during the fourth-innings chase in Cape Town that drew the strongest criticism. Poor shot selection and decision-making contributed to their collapse, prompting former players to question the team's performance."I'm just upset, it's terrible, it's un-Australian. There's no fight whatsoever, it's disgraceful," Warner said during television commentary."Chasing 288, you're winning a Test match, you could win a series, it's on the line, and this is the way that they're playing."I think it's deplorable but the batters have let the bowlers down the whole series."Former Australia batter Mark Waugh also criticised the team's approach. Waugh was part of the Australian side that completed a record run chase at Newlands in 2002."That was a terrible two hours of batting. That was immature … it was terrible," he said. "The shot selection, the technique and the execution was not good enough."Australia's batting concerns have been building for some time. Since Warner retired in 2024, followed by his long-time opening partner Usman Khawaja, the team have struggled to settle on a regular opening pair. Nic Maddinson was the latest batter to get an opportunity but failed to make an impression in South Africa.Marnus Labuschagne's latest failure at No. 3 could also put his Test future in doubt. He has received several opportunities from the selectors despite his recent struggles.There were, however, some positives for Australia. Matt Renshaw made the most of his recall by scoring 190 in the first Test while batting at No. 5. He also scored 74 alongside Travis Head, who opened the batting, in the third Test.With Steve Smith ruled out of the Cape Town Test due to a neck injury, Josh Inglis came into the side and scored a century.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Five takeaways for England after epic series
articles.summary: With both sides to face over the next 12 months, what can England take from South Africa and Australia's enthralling Test series?
articles.body:
If England fans were in any doubt over the difficulty of this winter's trip to South Africa, they should be no more.

The superb Proteas completed victory on the final day of their enthralling series against Australia to reaffirm their status as the best side in the world.

The contest was packed with subplots, many of which are relevant to England for their forthcoming tour and next summer's Ashes series beyond.

Captain Pat Cummins maintained Australia were still a "really good side" after the defeat.

It is undeniable, however, that they stand at an intriguing point in their development.

Knocked off the top of the Test rankings for the first time in two and a half years, they have an ageing bowling attack and a batting line-up caught between generations.

And for the first time in his career there is attention on Cummins himself.

One third of Australia's iconic pace trio, with Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood, he went more than 62 overs without a wicket between the second innings of the first Test and South Africa's second dig in the third. Only once has he finished a series with a worse bowling average than the 53.66 he returned in South Africa.

His expected wickets return of 29.6 suggests he bowled better than those figures suggest, but he has only returned a higher mark on that metric once in his past 20 series.

Of course, Cummins has plenty of credit in the bank but questions are bound to be raised given his age.

Were the 33-year-old not captain, it may have been him under pressure from Scott Boland to play in the third Test.

His call to bowl first in Cape Town also proved poor and he was helpless tactically when South Africa's openers attacked on the first morning before correcting things after lunch.

Since Joe Root returned as Test skipper, England have not picked a frontline spinner and have instead favoured a four-man pace attack of Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

South Africa's victory in the third Test suggests they will need an alternative before long.

Off-spinner Simon Harmer, who once considered playing for England before opting for the country of his birth, took 10-120 to bowl the Proteas to victory in Cape Town - the venue of the third Test against England.

Newlands is not typically a spinner's surface but it turned big from the third day. The overall average amount of turn throughout the Test (4.35 degrees) was the fourth-highest in Cape Town on record. The Test a place ahead on the list was last year, against Pakistan.

Harmer was helped by having left-arm pace bowlers Starc and Marco Jansen creating footholes outside the right-handers' off stump throughout. Starc will not be a factor against England but Jansen will.

England's spin issues are longstanding, meaning there is no easy answer.

And whether they pick Shoaib Bashir, return to Jack Leach or Mason Crane or hand a debut to Nottinghamshire's Liam Patterson-White – the recent recipient of an England development contract - they will have stiff competition.

Since Harmer returned to Test cricket in 2022, no spinner has a better average anywhere in the world.

If England do pick a spinner, it will give them a chance to expose one weakness in South Africa's batting order. This could be needed, given the strength of South Africa's bowling attack with Harmer, Jansen and Kagiso Rabada, backed up by Wiaan Mulder.

Captain Temba Bavuma was out to off-spin in four out of his five innings against Australia. The exception, the second Test when he made an epic 179 to turn the series on its head, came when Australia left out their premier tweaker Nathan Lyon.

Until the start of 2025, Bavuma averaged 46.85 against spin but his record has since dropped to 21.37. That drops to 15.00 against off-spin and 12.16 when such bowlers are coming over the wicket.

More broadly, and despite victory, South Africa's problems against the short ball were laid bare again in the third Test when seven of their wickets came when playing the hook or pull.

It is a problem that has often hampered England but West Indies and Afghanistan are the only sides averaging worse against short balls in Tests over the past four years.

Another trend to emerge from Australia's visit was the importance of lower-order runs.

In their first-Test victory, Australia added 266 runs after the sixth wicket fell in their first innings.

In the second Test, South Africa added 315 in the same period while in the second innings of the third Test they added 206 for the last five wickets - something that effectively won them the Test and series.

With the ball repeatedly getting soft as innings wore on, wicket-taking became more difficult.

Wickets fell once every 60 balls after the ball was 40 overs old in this series, compared to once every 37 balls in England's series against New Zealand earlier in the summer.

In recent years, England's lower order have attacked in an attempt to score quick runs.

This series showed the benefit of the lower-order batting time, sticking around for the top-order batters and stretching out an innings.

One of Australia's positives from their series defeat was the batting of Matt Renshaw.

In his first full series since his recall, he was the highest run-scorer at an average of 61.50.

With issues to solve elsewhere - most notably at number three where Marnus Labuschagne has gone 49 innings without a Test century and now looks likely to lose his place - Renshaw batted well enough to be given an extended run at the top of the order.

His 190 in the first Test came at number five, but 74 in the third as opener suggested Australia's long-running bid to replace David Warner may finally be over.

Before the Ashes next summer, England face Australia in the one-off 150th anniversary Test in Melbourne in March.

Root's men, under the new leadership of Stephen Fleming, can use that match to test plans to dismiss Renshaw.

While the left-hander was born in Yorkshire, he has never played against England. He averages a solid 42.69 in first-class cricket in the County Championship.

England will need to locate a weakness by the time the Ashes begins.

articles.title: 'WTC win was no fluke': Temba Bavuma slams 'critics' after statement win over Australia
articles.summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma believes his team have answered questions about their World Test Championship (WTC) triumph after completing a 2-1
articles.body: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma believes his team have answered questions about their World Test Championship (WTC) triumph after completing a 2-1 series win over Australia. The Proteas came back from a defeat in the opening Test to win the next two matches, including the series decider by 176 runs at Newlands on Saturday.South Africa's recent run includes qualifying for the 2025 WTC final even after forfeiting a series in New Zealand, beating defending champions Australia in the final at Lord's, drawing a series in Pakistan and winning a Test series in India for the first time in 25 years. They have now added a home series victory over Australia to that record.The win in Cape Town also took South Africa to the top of the ICC Test rankings. Simon Harmer played a key role in the victory, taking 6/16 in the second innings and finishing with match figures of 10/120. Kagiso Rabada claimed three early wickets as Australia were bowled out for 111 while chasing 288.South Africa's series win came after they lost the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs. They responded with an innings-and-31-run victory in Gqeberha before sealing the series in Cape Town.Speaking after the win, Bavuma reflected on the demands of the series and the effort required from his players to maintain their performance."It's tough, to be honest," he said. "You wake up every day asking yourself to be at your best. Physically, there's times where you feel like you can't go at 100%, but you need to dig deep, and if the opportunity's there, make sure you're in the best mental space to make the play for the team. Even if things don't go well for you with the ball or the bat, you still need to be looking at ways as to how you can contribute within the team."Bavuma described the series as "15 days of just pressure". It came after South Africa had gone almost a year without playing a Test and 21 months without playing one at home. He said the opening defeat in Durban had been a "rude awakening"."There were two quality sides who came up against each other, and really forced each other to play their best cricket," Bavuma said. "It will be important for us to acknowledge what we've achieved, celebrate whatever milestones, take whatever learnings that come with it, and really bask in what we've achieved. In the two-and-a-half years, if you look at the team, we've been able to squeeze out every inch of every individual."Bavuma also hopes the team's performances will change how they are viewed by critics, who have questioned whether their WTC title was a one-off achievement."I do hope with the way that we've performed, not the result, but the way that we've performed, it's given that belief. And I guess in a cheeky way, answer to certain critics saying that what we did at the WTC was a fluke. The sky's the limit for the team."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ishan Kishan breaks Suryakumar Yadav's record with historic T20I run spree, joins elite 2,000-run club
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan continued his remarkable run in T20I cricket, rewriting the Indian record books with an impressive half-century in the fifth and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan continued his remarkable run in T20I cricket, rewriting the Indian record books with an impressive half-century in the fifth and final match against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The left-handed batter surpassed Suryakumar Yadav's record for most runs by an Indian in a calendar year in T20Is, while also completing 2,000 runs in the format.Kishan brought up the landmark with an aggressive 61 off just 32 balls, featuring five sixes and as many fours. He now has 1,220 runs in 37 matches and innings in 2026, surpassing Suryakumar's previous record of 1,164 runs, which he had accumulated in 2022.Kishan has been in outstanding form throughout the year, averaging 35.88 at a strike rate of 171.58. His tally includes a century and eight half-centuries, underlining his consistency and attacking approach in the shortest format.The 28-year-old also became the seventh Indian to cross 2,000 runs in T20Is, reaching the milestone in his 69th innings. He is the third-fastest Indian to achieve the feat in terms of balls faced, having taken just 1,345 deliveries to get there.Only Abhishek Sharma (1,024 balls) and Suryakumar Yadav (1,164 balls) have reached 2,000 T20I runs quicker in terms of deliveries among Indian batters.Fewest balls to 2000 T20I runs (India)1024 - Abhishek Sharma1164 - Suryakumar Yadav1345 - Ishan KishanIshan Kishan overtakes Suryakumar Yadav's recordSuryakumar had set the benchmark in 2022 with 1,164 runs in 31 matches at an average of 46.56 and a strike rate of 187.43. Kishan went past that mark with his latest innings, taking his 2026 tally to 1,220 runs.His prolific year has also been fuelled by his contribution to India's title-winning campaign at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, where he scored 317 runs. The wicketkeeper-batter has carried that form into the bilateral assignments, establishing himself as one of India's most productive performers in the format.Kishan's 2,000-run milestone also puts him in an elite group of Indian T20I batters. He has scored 2,016 runs in 69 matches, with 206 fours and 96 sixes.In terms of innings taken to reach 2,000 runs, Virat Kohli and Suryakumar lead the Indian list, having achieved the feat in 56 innings each. KL Rahul reached the landmark in 58 innings, while Abhishek Sharma took 64. Kishan completed it in his 69th innings to occupy fifth place on that list.Kishan, Shreyas Iyer rescue India after early setbacksKishan's record-breaking knock came at a crucial stage after India suffered an early collapse. Asked to bat first after New Zealand won the toss, the visitors struck early, with Adam Milne dismissing Abhishek Sharma in the second over.Kishan, coming in at number three, responded with an attacking approach and joined Shreyas Iyer in rebuilding the innings. The pair added 107 runs for the third wicket in little more than seven overs, giving India the momentum after the early setbacks.Kishan initially took time to settle before shifting gears, while Iyer was aggressive from the outset. The India batter struck four sixes and three fours during his 50 off 23 deliveries, registering another valuable contribution in the middle order.Kishan brought up his half-century off 28 balls with a six off Michael Bracewell. Iyer soon followed, reaching his fifty in 22 deliveries.New Zealand, however, fought back by removing both set batters in quick succession. Blair Tickner dismissed Kishan, who was caught at deep mid-wicket, before Iyer fell to Adam Milne.Naman Dhir added 33 off 23 balls, while Nitish Kumar Reddy contributed 22 off 17 deliveries as India finished with 191/8.India had already secured an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match series heading into the final encounter.India's leading T20I run-scorers: Rohit Sharma tops the overall charts with 4,231 runs, followed by Virat Kohli (4,188) and Suryakumar Yadav (3,272). Among active Indian batters, Suryakumar remains ahead, with Hardik Pandya (2,288), Abhishek Sharma (2,268) and KL Rahul (2,265) also having crossed the 2,000-run mark.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Abki baar 400 paar: India unleash six-hitting assault, set new world record in 2026
articles.summary: India became the first team in cricket history to hit 400 sixes in a calendar year during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in
articles.body: India became the first team in cricket history to hit 400 sixes in a calendar year during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday.The milestone came in India's 40th match of 2026, when the batters struck 11 sixes to take their tally for the year to exactly 400. The previous record belonged to Austria, who hit 326 sixes in 2025. Among full-member nations, India's previous best was 289 sixes in 2022, also across 40 matches. Their average has therefore risen from 7.2 sixes per match in 2022 to 10 this year.All-rounder Naman Dhir hit the 400th six, top-edging a flick off Blair Tickner over the fine-leg boundary in the 19th over. India finished their innings at 191/8, with Ishan Kishan hitting five sixes during his 61 off 32 balls, Shreyas Iyer adding four in his 50 off 23 deliveries and Nitish Kumar Reddy contributing another six.India have also set a record for the most sixes against a single opponent in a calendar year. Of their 400 sixes in 2026, 142 have come against New Zealand.Abhishek Sharma has led India's six-hitting tally with 86, followed by Kishan with 60 and Sanju Samson with 50.The Indian innings went through three phases, starting with an early loss of wickets before Iyer and Kishan put together a strong partnership in the middle overs. Their stand of 107 runs came in just over seven overs and helped India recover from the early setbacks.Both batters found their rhythm despite some assistance for the pacers from the pitch. However, New Zealand, led by Adam Milne's four-wicket haul, pulled things back towards the end to restrict India to 191/8 in their 20 overs.India had already taken an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match series heading into the final game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tim Seifert, Glenn Phillips power New Zealand to 7-wicket win in the final T20I as India take series 3-2
articles.summary: India clinched the five-match T20I series 3-2 despite suffering a seven-wicket defeat against New Zealand in the final match at Seddon Park in Hamilton on
articles.body: India clinched the five-match T20I series 3-2 despite suffering a seven-wicket defeat against New Zealand in the final match at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. Tim Seifert and Glenn Phillips produced commanding performances with the bat to guide the hosts to a comfortable victory after Adam Milne's four-wicket haul restricted India to 191/8.After being asked to bat first by New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner, India recovered from an early collapse to post a competitive total, courtesy of explosive half-centuries from Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer.Kishan smashed 61 off 32 deliveries, while Iyer contributed 50 off just 23 balls as the duo stitched together a crucial 93-run partnership for the third wicket. However, Milne's impressive spell of 4/19 helped New Zealand pull things back towards the end of the Indian innings. In reply, Seifert led the chase with a magnificent 93, while Phillips remained unbeaten on 65 to take New Zealand home with 17 balls to spare.Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer rescue India after early setbacksIndia did not get off to the best of starts after being put in to bat, with Jacob Duffy keeping things tight in the opening over before Adam Milne struck in the second. The New Zealand pacer dismissed Abhishek Sharma for just one run, with Daryl Mitchell completing the catch.Sanju Samson's difficult run continued as he departed for four off 10 deliveries, leaving India struggling at 19/2 in 3.1 overs.However, Kishan and Iyer brought India back into the contest with an aggressive partnership. The duo took on the New Zealand bowling attack, finding boundaries regularly and putting pressure on the hosts. Kishan brought up his half-century in 28 balls, while Iyer matched his aggression at the other end. Their 93-run stand helped India recover from a precarious position and cross the 100-run mark comfortably.The 10th over proved particularly expensive for New Zealand as Iyer and Kishan took Michael Bracewell apart, collecting 27 runs. Iyer struck two sixes and a four, while Kishan added a six and a boundary. However, Blair Tickner eventually ended Kishan's innings, with Nathan Smith completing the catch. The wicketkeeper-batter departed for 61 off 32 deliveries, including five fours and five sixes.Iyer continued his attacking approach and brought up his half-century in just 22 balls. However, he too fell shortly afterwards, scoring 50 off 23 deliveries with three fours and four sixes.Adam Milne's four-wicket haul restricts India to 191With both set batters back in the pavilion, India struggled to maintain the same scoring momentum in the latter stages. Tilak Varma departed for six, while Naman Dhir and Nitish Kumar Reddy attempted to provide the finishing touches.Dhir played a useful knock of 33 off 23 balls, hitting four boundaries and a six. Nitish contributed 22 off 17 deliveries as the pair helped India move towards the 200-run mark. However, New Zealand's bowlers struck at regular intervals towards the end. Tickner removed Dhir, while Phillips took a good catch to dismiss Nitish. Milne then picked up his fourth wicket by removing Bhuvneshwar Kumar for six.India eventually finished at 191/8 in their allotted 20 overs. Milne was the standout bowler for New Zealand, returning figures of 4/19, while Tickner and Smith also chipped in with two wickets each.Tim Seifert, Glenn Phillips power New Zealand's chaseChasing 192, New Zealand suffered an early setback when Arshdeep Singh dismissed Finn Allen for two in the second over. The left-arm pacer produced an extra bounce, forcing Allen to mistime his pull shot before Ishan Kishan completed the catch at midwicket.However, Seifert and Daryl Mitchell steadied the innings with a crucial partnership. Seifert initially struggled to find his timing but made the most of a reprieve after being dropped by Naman Dhir on 13. The New Zealand opener gradually found his rhythm and accelerated once the initial movement disappeared. Seifert brought up a superb half-century and combined with Mitchell to add 73 runs for the second wicket.Varun Chakaravarthy eventually broke the partnership by dismissing Mitchell, but that proved to be India's final breakthrough.Glenn Phillips joined Seifert in the middle, and the pair took complete control of the chase. Phillips continued his impressive run with the bat, scoring an unbeaten 65 off 38 deliveries, while Seifert remained the mainstay of the innings with his 93. The duo kept finding boundaries and ensured there was no late drama as New Zealand reached 195/3 in 18 overs, winning the match by seven wickets.India clinch series despite final-match defeatAlthough New Zealand finished the series with back-to-back victories, India had done enough earlier in the contest to secure the five-match T20I series 3-2.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We were a bit sloppy': Shreyas Iyer points out India's mistakes after 5th T20I defeat against New Zealand
articles.summary: India captain Shreyas Iyer admitted that his team fell short in all three departments after suffering a seven-wicket defeat against New Zealand in the
articles.body: India captain Shreyas Iyer admitted that his team fell short in all three departments after suffering a seven-wicket defeat against New Zealand in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. Despite clinching the five-match series 3-2, Iyer pointed to India's inability to maintain momentum with the bat, coupled with an underwhelming bowling and fielding display, as key reasons behind the defeat.India posted 191/8 after being asked to bat first, with Ishan Kishan and Iyer producing impressive half-centuries. However, the visitors failed to capitalise on their strong recovery after losing both set batters in quick succession.New Zealand made the most of India's shortcomings in the field and chased down the target in just 17.4 overs. Tim Seifert led the charge with a blistering 93 off 50 deliveries, while Glenn Phillips remained unbeaten on 65 off 38 balls to guide the hosts to a comfortable seven-wicket victory.Speaking at the post-match presentation, Iyer acknowledged that India could have done better after building a promising platform with the bat."It was plausible, honestly. We could have been better considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I created the momentum. And then from there on we lost back-to-back wickets. And then suddenly pressure on the new batsman," Iyer said.Shreyas Iyer rues India's batting collapse after strong partnershipIyer and Kishan added 93 runs for the third wicket after India were reduced to 19/2 early in the innings. Kishan scored 61 off 32 balls, while the Indian skipper contributed 50 off just 23 deliveries.The duo helped India recover from a difficult position and put the visitors on course for a total in excess of 200. However, their dismissals in quick succession disrupted India's momentum and allowed New Zealand to regain control.Iyer also highlighted the nature of the surface, explaining how the movement and variable bounce made batting challenging, particularly against deliveries directed at a hard length."It wasn't an easy wicket to play on, especially when the ball was seaming and holding a bit. And also skidding through at times. You must have seen a couple of us; Tilak and I got out in a similar fashion. So yeah, it was challenging, especially with that hard length. But to get to 194, yeah, it was reasonable, I feel. I think we still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. We were a bit sloppy," he added.Iyer admits India need to improve their fieldingIndia's fielding lapses also proved costly during New Zealand's chase. Naman Dhir dropped Seifert when the opener was batting on 13, allowing him to make the most of the reprieve and go on to score a match-winning 93.Sanju Samson also missed an opportunity to dismiss Phillips after failing to hold on to a sharp outside edge in the 15th over. Iyer admitted that fielding remains an area where India need to improve, while acknowledging the challenges of playing under different conditions in New Zealand."So, I feel today was just that opportunity which we wanted to capitalise on, but we couldn't. But we can brainstorm, and we have to work on a couple of things, especially fielding. That is one aspect of the game we need to improve on," he said."But honestly, it's not that easy when you come under such dark lights, clear skies. We don't get that much in India. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had a strong message about his team's approach to handling pressure after India clinched the five-match T20I series against New Zealand 3-2, insisting that fear has no place in his dictionary."There is no word like “dar” (fear) in my dictionary and directory," Gambhir said at the post-series press conference after India's series victory.The former India opener also praised his players for the way they responded to challenging circumstances, particularly in the opening match, when they secured a win despite a demanding travel schedule and limited preparation time.“The way our boys handled pressure, winning the first game after a 15-hour flight and one practice session was commendable,” Gambhir said.India won the first three matches to take an unassailable lead in the series before New Zealand bounced back with victories in the final two encounters. The 3-2 result nevertheless gave India a series triumph away from home, with Gambhir highlighting the team's ability to embrace pressure rather than retreat from it.Gambhir on Rishabh Pant's injury updateGambhir was also asked about Rishabh Pant's availability, but the India head coach did not have a definitive update on the wicketkeeper-batter."I don’t have an update yet on Rishabh Pant, will share when I get," Gambhir said.The comment left Pant's immediate availability uncertain, with the team awaiting further information on his condition.Shreyas Iyer identifies areas India need to improveIndia captain Shreyas Iyer acknowledged that there were areas of concern despite the series victory, particularly bowling and fielding, after the visitors lost the final two matches."We still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Mumbai look for fourth win on the trot
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Mumbai have started their Ranji Trophy campaign with three bonus-point wins on the trot and there is no chance of relenting when they square off
articles.body: MUMBAI: Mumbai have started their Ranji Trophy campaign with three bonus-point wins on the trot and there is no chance of relenting when they square off against Railways at the Brabourne Stadium from Monday.Mumbai kicked off the 2026-27 campaign under new skipper Siddhesh Lad with an innings-and-155-run win over Chandigarh. The 42-time champions then toppled Himachal Pradesh by an innings and 97 runs in an away match before recording a 10-wicket victory over Haryana in their last outing.The secret behind their rollicking start lies in contributions coming from all quarters. In the first game against Chandigarh, India players Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan got out cheaply, but others rallied to help Mumbai post 429 in the first innings. Tushar Deshpande then turned up the heat with a five-wicket haul, including a hat-trick, to rattle the visitors, from which they never recovered.In the second game, Deshpande once again led the charge with figures of four for 46 as Mumbai bowled out Himachal Pradesh for 140 in the first innings. Mumbai then posted 528/8 declared thanks to centuries from Sarfaraz Khan (154) and Akash Anand (117*), before Mohit Avasthi's 5/44 ensured Mumbai did not have to bat again.In the last game at the BKC ground against Haryana, Angkrish Raghuvanshi (114) and Musheer Khan (109) struck centuries to help the home side post 430 in the first innings. Musheer (6/85) then rolled his arm over to run through the Haryana line-up and help Mumbai enforce the follow-on. In the second innings, it was Tanush Kotian's turn to display his wares as the off-spinner claimed 8/81, his best first-class figures, to ensure a result remained possible. Raghuvanshi (67*) and Divyaansh Saxena (30*) then sealed a 10-wicket win and another bonus point for Mumbai.While Mumbai have garnered 21 points from three games, Railways' campaign has struggled to take off, with just two points in their kitty. In the first two games, they conceded first-innings leads before losing to Tamil Nadu by five wickets in their last outing.While it is technically Railways' home match with them picking CCI as their venue, the real advantage lies with Mumbai, whose players have featured extensively at the historic venue in local cricket.Mumbai opener Divyaansh Saxena feels that will play into his side's hands. "It's a good opportunity for everyone. We have been playing at CCI since childhood and it's actually a home game for us. We know the wicket well and how it will pan out over the next four days."That, however, does not mean Mumbai will take it easy. On the contrary, Saxena said: "Yes, we have got bonus-point wins, but everyone is looking forward to finishing the first half of the Ranji Trophy well before we move on to the white-ball tournaments."For Railways skipper Bhargav Merai, the team is missing the final push that can turn competitive performances into victories. "We have been competing well, but the push isn't coming and we aren't able to finish games. Hopefully, if we get into a good position in this game against Mumbai and grab our chances, the result may go in our favour," said Merai.Mumbai retain same squadWith Shardul Thakur still sidelined by injury, the Mumbai selection committee, led by Rajesh Pawar, decided to stick with the same 16-member squad. The 34-year-old has been sidelined since sustaining the injury during a training session ahead of the season's opening round.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Please listen now': Mohammad Yousuf's blunt advice to Babar Azam amid prolonged batting slump
articles.summary: Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf has urged Babar Azam to travel to Australia or South Africa and work with specialist coaches to address the
articles.body: Former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf has urged Babar Azam to travel to Australia or South Africa and work with specialist coaches to address the technical flaws in his batting, warning that playing first-class cricket without fixing those issues could further dent the star batter's confidence.Yousuf believes Babar needs focused, specialised coaching to rediscover his best form, rather than relying solely on domestic cricket to prepare for international assignments.Babar's struggles were once again under the spotlight during Pakistan's run chase against Sri Lanka in the tri-series final on Saturday. Although Pakistan went on to win the tournament, Babar failed to make a significant contribution."He should be going to South Africa or Australia and just focusing on working on his batting now. That will help him," Yousuf said in a post on social media on Sunday.The former Pakistan captain also questioned Babar's decision to turn out in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, where he is scheduled to represent Lahore from November 3, ahead of the two-Test series against Sri Lanka beginning on November 9.'I said this four years ago, and nobody listened'In a strongly worded post on X, Yousuf called for Babar to receive specialised coaching in England or Australia before returning to first-class cricket."I don't think BabarAzam should be playing first class cricket until he fixes his technical issues through specialized coaching. Struggling in domestic cricket could further harm his confidence and career. Send him to an academy in England or Australia. He is still Pakistan's top player, and with the right guidance and a little effort, he can return to his best. I said this four years ago, and nobody listened. Please listen now," Yousuf wrote.The advice comes at a crucial stage in Babar's career. The 32-year-old has scored only one century in the last three years in ODIs, despite having 20 hundreds in the format. He has already been dropped from Pakistan's T20I setup, while his place in the white-ball squads has come under scrutiny.If Babar is to be considered for Pakistan's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, a significant turnaround in form will be crucial.Former Pakistan players divided over Babar's strugglesBabar's decline has remained a major talking point, particularly after the standards he set between 2018 and 2023, when he established himself among the leading batters in world cricket. His performances since stepping down as captain following the 2023 ODI World Cup, however, have not matched those levels.Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis recently said on a podcast that Babar had been unfortunate to be the best batter in the side and had not received the support he needed from his teammates.Retired all-rounder Imad Wasim has also defended Babar, saying he had never seen a Pakistan player face as much criticism and hate from the media, critics and social media users.With Pakistan's next T20I assignment and the 2027 ODI World Cup on the horizon, Babar faces mounting pressure to rediscover his form.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
